text: Only partly, I think. Exams are fair in the sense that everyone answers the same questions under the same conditions. But they mostly test memory and how well you perform under pressure on one particular day. A student who's brilliant at research or teamwork might not shine in a two-hour written test, so I'd say exams show part of the picture, not all of it.

tips.en: Fair in the sense that specifies exactly how exams are fair.
tips.kk: Fair in the sense that … — емтиханның нақты неден әділ екенін нақтылайсыз.
tips.ru: Fair in the sense that … — уточняете, в чём именно экзамен честный.
tips.example: Exams are fair in the sense that

tips.en: Part of the picture, not all of it is a memorable summary.
tips.kk: Part of the picture, not all of it — есте қалатын қорытынды.
tips.ru: Part of the picture, not all of it — запоминающийся итог.
tips.example: exams show part of the picture

questions.question: Are exams a fair way to measure students’ abilities?

text: In many ways, yes. When work is assessed throughout the year, students have to keep up with the material instead of cramming everything in the last two weeks. It also gives a more accurate picture of someone's progress. The risk is that it can be harder to check whether students did the work themselves, especially now that AI tools can write essays.

tips.en: Instead of cramming everything shows what is avoided.
tips.kk: Instead of cramming everything — неден құтылуға болатынын көрсетесіз.
tips.ru: Instead of cramming everything — показываете, чего удаётся избежать.
tips.example: instead of cramming everything in the last two weeks

tips.en: Especially now that AI tools makes the answer feel up to date.
tips.kk: Especially now that AI tools … — өзекті дерек жауапты жаңа етеді.
tips.ru: Especially now that AI tools … — актуальная деталь делает ответ свежим.
tips.example: especially now that AI tools can write essays

note.en: “Studying a lot at the last minute”.

questions.question: Is it better to assess students throughout the year rather than with final exams?

text: Mostly because the stakes are so high. If one exam decides your university place or your scholarship, the temptation to cheat becomes enormous, especially for students who feel they haven't prepared well. Pressure from parents plays a part too. I don't think stricter punishments alone solve the problem; making exams less decisive would probably reduce cheating more effectively.

tips.en: The stakes are so high is the one cause everything else follows from.
tips.kk: The stakes are so high — қалғанының бәрі шығатын бір себеп.
tips.ru: The stakes are so high — одна причина, из которой вытекает всё остальное.
tips.example: Mostly because the stakes are so high

tips.en: Making exams less decisive challenges the obvious answer of harsher punishment.
tips.kk: Making exams less decisive — «қатаң жазалау» деген айқын жауаппен дауласасыз.
tips.ru: Making exams less decisive — вы спорите с очевидным ответом «строже наказывать».
tips.example: making exams less decisive would probably reduce cheating more effectively

questions.question: Why do some students cheat in exams?

text: I don't think so. Putting everything on a single test means that one bad day — an illness or simply nerves — can change someone's whole future. Universities could also consider school grades, a personal statement or an interview, as they do in many countries. That would be fairer, although it would take more time and might be harder to keep free from corruption.

tips.en: One bad day can change someone's whole future is a strong argument based on consequences.
tips.kk: One bad day … can change someone's whole future — салдары арқылы күшті дәлел.
tips.ru: One bad day … can change someone's whole future — сильный довод через последствие.

tips.en: Although it would take more time admits a weakness in your own proposal.
tips.kk: Although it would take more time — өз ұсынысыңыздың кемшілігін мойындайсыз.
tips.ru: Although it would take more time — признаёте минус своего же предложения.
tips.example: although it would take more time

note.en: “A written text about yourself and your goals”.

questions.followUp: What else should universities look at?
questions.question: Should one exam decide whether a student can go to university?

text: Personally, I'm against formal exams at that age. Young children learn best through curiosity and play, and grading them too early can make them anxious or convince them that they're bad at a subject before they've really started. Teachers obviously need to check progress, but they can do that through observation and short informal tasks rather than tests with marks.

tips.en: I'm against formal exams at that age gives the opinion straight away.
tips.kk: I'm against formal exams at that age — пікір бірінші сөйлемде.
tips.ru: I'm against formal exams at that age — мнение в первой фразе.
tips.example: I'm against formal exams at that age

tips.en: Through observation and short informal tasks says not only “no” but also “how else”.
tips.kk: Through observation and short informal tasks — тек «жоқ» емес, «басқаша қалай» дегенге де жауап.
tips.ru: Through observation and short informal tasks — не только «нет», но и «как иначе».
tips.example: through observation and short informal tasks
